question_text: If the core and cladding of an optical fibre have refractive indexes $1.39$ and $1.3$ respectively, its numerical aperture will be approximately
solution: The numerical aperture (NA) of an optical fibre is given by $\text{NA} = \sqrt{\mu_{\text{core}}^2 - \mu_{\text{cladding}}^2} = \sqrt{(1.39)^2 - (1.3)^2} = \sqrt{1.9321 - 1.69} = \sqrt{0.2421} \approx 0.492 \approx 0.5$.

question_text: At what angle a ray of light should be incident on face $AB$ so that it retraces its path after reflection from the silvered face $AC$?
diagram_description: A triangular prism $ABC$ with vertex angle $A = 30^\circ$ and refractive index $\mu = \sqrt{2}$. The face $AC$ is silvered. A ray of light is incident on face $AB$ at an angle of incidence $i$, refracts, and strikes face $AC$ perpendicularly.
solution: For the ray to retrace its path, it must strike the silvered surface $AC$ normally, so the angle of incidence at face $AC$ is $r_2 = 0^\circ$. Since $r_1 + r_2 = A$, we have $r_1 = A = 30^\circ$. Using Snell's law at face $AB$: $\sin i = \mu \sin r_1 = \sqrt{2} \sin 30^\circ = \sqrt{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \implies i = 45^\circ$.

question_text: A bulb is placed at a depth of $2\sqrt{7}\text{ m}$ inside water and a floating opaque disc is placed over the bulb so that the bulb is not visible from the surface. The minimum diameter of the disc is (Refractive index of water is $4/3$)
solution: The minimum radius of the circular disc to prevent light from emerging is $r = \frac{h}{\sqrt{\mu^2 - 1}} = \frac{2\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{(4/3)^2 - 1}} = \frac{2\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{7}/3} = 6\text{ m}$. Thus, the minimum diameter is $D = 2r = 12\text{ m}$.

question_text: An object and a plane mirror are approaching each other with speeds of $2\text{ m/sec}$ and $1\text{ m/sec}$ respectively. The velocity of the image with respect to ground will be
solution: Let the direction of motion of the object be positive ($v_O = +2\text{ m/s}$) and the mirror be negative ($v_M = -1\text{ m/s}$). Using the relation $v_I - v_M = -(v_O - v_M)$, we get $v_I = 2v_M - v_O = 2(-1) - 2 = -4\text{ m/s}$. Hence, the speed of the image is $4\text{ m/sec}$ approaching the object.

question_text: An object is placed at $50\text{ cm}$ from a concave mirror of focal length $25\text{ cm}$. The image is
options: Real, inverted and same in size
solution: The radius of curvature is $R = 2f = 2 \times 25\text{ cm} = 50\text{ cm}$. Since the object is placed at the center of curvature ($u = R = 50\text{ cm}$), the image formed is real, inverted, at the center of curvature, and of the same size as the object.

question_text: The focal length of a convex lens is $20\text{ cm}$. An object is placed at a distance $50\text{ cm}$ from it. The ratio of the size of the real image to the object is
solution: Using the magnification formula for a lens with $u = -50\text{ cm}$ and $f = +20\text{ cm}$: $m = \frac{f}{u + f} = \frac{20}{-50 + 20} = -\frac{20}{30} = -\frac{2}{3}$. The magnitude of the ratio of the size of the image to the object is $\frac{2}{3}$.

question_text: The value of $\mu_{21} \times \mu_{32} \times \mu_{43} \times \mu_{14}$ will be (symbols have their usual meaning)
solution: By the principle of reversibility and successive refractions, $\mu_{ji} = \frac{\mu_j}{\mu_i}$. Therefore, $\mu_{21} \times \mu_{32} \times \mu_{43} \times \mu_{14} = \frac{\mu_2}{\mu_1} \times \frac{\mu_3}{\mu_2} \times \frac{\mu_4}{\mu_3} \times \frac{\mu_1}{\mu_4} = 1$.
